title: Observational Astronomy
description: Everything known about the sky came through a lens. A bigger mirror gathers more light and splits finer detail; up to the limit that the wave nature of light itself sets. Unlocks the Telescope Mirror Blank.

puzzle.goal: Light from a distant star enters a round mirror of diameter D. Because light is a wave, the mirror cannot focus it to a point: it makes a small disc with rings, and two stars closer together than that disc cannot be told apart. Write the smallest angle θ the mirror resolves for light of wavelength λ.
puzzle.name: Diffraction limit of a circular aperture
puzzle.ask: Find θ in arcseconds for green light, λ in micrometres and D in metres.
puzzle.method: The first dark ring of the diffraction pattern of a circular opening sits where the first zero of the Bessel function J₁ falls; 1 radian is 206,265 arcseconds.
